newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia pipeline attacks cost $56 mln in '97.
newsitem.headline: Colombia pipeline attacks cost $56 mln in '97.

text.p: Leftist rebel attacks on the Cano Limon-Covenas have cost Colombia an estimated $56 million this year so far, state-run oil company Ecopetrol said Friday.

The pipeline, the second largest in the country with a 250,000 barrels per day pumping capacity, has been blown up at least 45 times by rebels of the Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN) this year.
The Cano Limon field in northeast Arauca province, operated by Occidental Petroleum Corp, was shut in twice in the space of less than a month in July and August.

Ecopetrol said in a statement that rebel attacks had caused at least $50 million in lost production so far this year and that pumping operations along the pipeline have been halted 49 days so far in 1997.

More than 140,000 barrels of crude, worth about $6 million, have been spilled in the attacks and repairs to the pipes have cost about $1.7 million. The bill for cleaning up the environmental damage is also put at about $1.7 million, Ecopetrol said.
The pipeline was blown up a total of 45 times in the whole of 1996.
